findings.what: The overview and node page say a node has 'no trail' when completeness is null. They ignore the compiler's trail flag, which TraceNode doesn't declare.
findings.why: The compiler emits nodes[*].trail (src/web/compiler/index.ts:228, pinned by data-4.test.ts). The screens decide 'no trail' from completeness === null instead (Overview.tsx:35 and :41-45, Node.tsx:10). A node in flight, with activity.jsonl or loop.jsonl but no README Completeness section, would be shown as having no trail, which is not what the trail holds (HONEST-1, DATA-8). It doesn't fire on the real build trail at HEAD, because every build node with a loop has a README, so this is non-blocking.

findings.what: TraceRule.status is typed string, but the compiler emits null for a rule with no matrix row.
findings.why: index.ts sets status to cells === null ? null : …, and data-1.test.ts asserts null. The loader type claims a string is always there. The screens happen to handle null as 'not built', but the type hides the case from the compiler's checks.

findings.what: The matrix links any non-empty PR cell as /pull/<text>, while the rule page links only a cell that matches ^#(\d+)$.
findings.why: NAV-3 and the react-web rule say links out are built from IDs in trace.json, never from free text. Every real PR cell today is '#<n>', so nothing is wrong on screen. But the two screens parse the same cell two ways, and a cell like 'pending' would become a GitHub link on the matrix.
